name: FL-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strongly Republican district (R+14) in Southwest Florida
Huge fundraising gap: Schwartzel raised $2.1M vs. Arias $58K
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot
Prediction markets price Republicans around 94% to hold the seat
model.rationale: The seat's R+14 lean, the retirement of Byron Donalds, and a lopsided money advantage for Republican Jim Schwartzel all point to the GOP holding this open seat. Markets agree, pricing a Democratic win at only about 6%, so the forecast stays firmly in Republican territory with modest room for uncertainty given no polling.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Arias or a divisive Republican primary aftermath that depresses GOP turnout could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Byron Donalds (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Byron Donalds is leaving this Southwest Florida seat to run for governor, creating an open-seat contest in a district that leans Republican by about fourteen points. Republican Jim Schwartzel has dominated the money race, raising roughly $2.1 million, while Democrat Victor Arias has raised under $60,000 and holds minimal cash. An independent candidate trails far behind in both fundraising and visibility.

With no public polling and no expert ratings, the picture rests on district fundamentals, the fundraising gap, and prediction markets, which give Republicans about a 94 percent chance of holding the seat. The race is rated Likely Republican, with the open-seat dynamic the main reason it is not rated Safe.
